result.paraphrase: Abstract During the COVID-19 crisis, fake news, conspiracy theories, and backlash against specific groups spread mainly through social media. This phenomenon has been called an “infodemic,” and this study analyzed the characteristics of the infodemic on Twitter. Typological attributes of the infodemic Twitter network showed “community cluster” features. Frequently shared domains and URLs displayed coherent patterns within the network. The leading domains and URLs were trustworthy information sources, popular blogs, and public health research institutions. Interestingly, the most shared conversational content in the network concerned a COVID-19-related incident at a church in Korea, rooted in misinformation and false belief.
